results.title: 10 Alternatives To The Tesla Roadster
results.content:
Gestalt Imagery / Shutterstock

The Model S may have been Tesla's introduction to the EV mass market, but it has evolved into so much more. The Model S Plaid adds another motor to the already powerful base Model S and produces a total of 1,020 horsepower, breaking records left, right, and center. It has a top speed of 200 mph and can go from 0-60 in just two seconds, a feat matched by very few other vehicles, be it EV or ICE-powered. The Model S Plaid achieves this while still maintaining the impressive range and luxury offered by the base Model S, giving a whole new meaning to the word 'supercar'. If you want the best of Tesla but don't see the Roadster coming out anytime soon, the Model S Plaid is a very viable alternative.

Related: 10 Electric Crossovers That Are Fun To Drive [...] Mike Mareen / Shutterstock

The Porsche Taycan is quite possibly the most well-rounded electric sports car you can buy and drive right now. Starting at around $88,000, the Taycan offers ferocious acceleration and sleek looks that are sure to turn heads no matter where you are driving. The base model produces 402 horsepower, but the highest spec Turbo S model cranks that all the way up to 750 horsepower and can go from 0-60 mph in just 2.4 seconds, which certainly puts the Porsche Taycan in the same category as the Tesla Roadster. The driving range tops out at up to 246 miles on a single charge, but the Porsche Taycan makes up for that in more ways than one, and you can configure it in a number of different ways to fit your liking.

## 2 Lucid Air Sapphire - $250,000 [...] Lucid

The Lucid Air may look inconspicuous with its four-door cabin, but the Sapphire trim is one of the quickest cars you can buy right now. Thanks to three electric motors, the Lucid Air Sapphire churns out a massive 1,200 horsepower and has beaten quite a few illustrious challengers in a straight-line race. Even if you don't want to fork out more than $250,000 for the Sapphire, you can still get some ridiculous performance numbers. The base Pure model produces 480 horsepower, the Touring version has 620 horsepower and the Grand Touring version has a whopping 1050 horsepower. Couple that with a 112.0-kWh battery pack providing the longest range in any EV, and you have a car that can give any other EV a run for its money, let alone the Tesla Roadster.

Only available with all-wheel drive, the R1S range starts with the $75,900 R1S Adventure Dual Standard, which has 270 miles of range from its 92.5 kWh battery, 533 hp from its two motors, and a 0 to 60 mph time of 4.5 seconds. The $82,900 R1S Adventure Dual Large gives you 109.4 kWh and 330 miles of range, 665 hp from a more powerful pair of motors, and a 3.4-second acceleration time. [...] If you want even more range, Rivian offers the $89,900 Adventure Dual Max, which has 141.5 kWh and a claimed range of 410 miles. Power and acceleration are identical to those of the Dual Large model. The new $105,900 R1S Ascend Tri Max with three drive units is more powerful at 850 hp than the outgoing quad-motor variant, with 850 hp and 2.9 seconds to sixty. It features the same 141.5 kWh Max battery pack for 371 miles of claimed range.

Rivian will introduce a new quad-motor R1S in 2025, the R1S Ascend Quad Max. Its four motors will deliver 1,025 hp and 1,198 lb-ft, enough to push the R1S to 60 mph in 2.6 seconds.

### BMW iX [...] Adding a second motor for all-wheel drive increases the price to $63,900, and the range is reduced to 280 miles. The quickest version is the $73,900 GT-Line, which has the same 379 hp as the other dual-motor variants but 516 lb-ft of torque compared to 443 lb-ft. This allows it to reach 60 mph from a standstill in 5 seconds, making it quick for such a big bus. It will become even quicker when the EV9 GT arrives on the scene.

### Rivian R1S

Rivian recently overhauled its R1 lineup, giving its vehicles new motors, batteries, features, and refinements over the previous version. Even though, at first glance, it looks virtually identical to the outgoing model, the manufacturer considers the new R1S the second generation of the vehicle, pointing out all the areas where it has been improved.
